entries.title: Comparison ledger
suitableFor: Repeated records with shared units and fields.
Operators need to scan several candidates before choosing one.
avoid: Image-led discovery with few comparable fields.
Hiding required values behind hover or selection.
entries.narrow: Proposed: keep the identity field with each labelled record; expose detail in a dedicated view when the table cannot fit. Preserve query and selected record on return.
states: Proposed: zero results with clear filters
Proposed: selected row and retained return
Proposed: loading and retry without losing scope
artDirection: Align quantities and units on a ruled baseline because comparisons depend on shared measures.
Use one restrained status accent; identity and numbers retain the strongest type hierarchy.
entries.tradeoff: Dense rows increase comparison capacity but leave little room for descriptive or visual differences. A focused list/detail view can reduce narrow-screen scanning.

entries.title: Input / result bench
suitableFor: An authored input is evaluated or transformed into a reviewable result.
A small number of parameters qualify the same action.
avoid: Unrelated monitoring metrics.
Irreversible actions without a separate review step.
entries.narrow: Proposed: stack input, parameters, submit and result in task order. Keep the submitted input available when a result or error appears; do not copy the upstream screenshot-only narrow treatment.
states: Proposed: pending result with retained input
Proposed: invalid input and local explanation
artDirection: Give input and result equal reading width because users compare the transformation.
Set parameters in a quieter labelled rail so their density does not compete with authored text.
entries.tradeoff: Paired regions support comparison but can demand too much horizontal space. A simple form with a separate result page is often clearer for infrequent work.

entries.title: Summary to evidence
suitableFor: A summary raises a question that a trend and underlying records can answer.
A team revisits the same stable measures over time.
avoid: Decorative metrics that do not connect to actionable evidence.
Time-critical queues where a large overview delays the next item.
entries.narrow: Proposed: retain scope before measures, then chart and records in reading order. Reduce chart detail rather than shrinking labels; expose its values as readable text.
artDirection: Share unit labels and number formatting across summary, trend and records to make the evidence relationship visible.
Use a single highlight for the selected period, keeping surrounding data quiet enough to compare.
entries.tradeoff: A summary makes periodic review faster but adds a layer between operator and record. Its added complexity needs a real decision that the overview supports.

entries.title: Object beside conditions
suitableFor: A single object needs both close visual inspection and explicit purchase conditions.
Differences in scale, material or fit affect the decision.
avoid: Invented product imagery or unverified specifications.
Long unrelated content between the price and action.
entries.narrow: Proposed: show a useful object view, then title, price, options and complete conditions. Keep captions with images and make the purchase action reachable without a fixed overlay covering content.
states: Proposed: changed price and complete total
artDirection: Give the object more area only when its visible details answer a buying question; label schematics as schematics.
Connect ruled specifications to the options and complete cost so the visual object and purchase conditions stay one decision.
entries.tradeoff: An object-led sheet can communicate material and construction but delay fit and action. A familiar compact product page is equally valid when imagery provides little additional evidence.

entries.title: Options before commitment
suitableFor: A finite set of options changes availability or the final commitment.
Customers need to inspect conditions before confirming.
avoid: Assuming a booking engine, taxes or validation exist because a product component has options.
Hiding a changed total until after submission.
entries.narrow: Proposed: keep required groups in one vertical order. Place each error beside its group and present the updated total before the action; preserve valid choices after failure.
artDirection: Use explicit group labels and quiet separators because option dependency matters more than a dramatic layout.
Give the complete total and commitment a shared typographic level so the cost is read with the action.
entries.tradeoff: A linear stack makes dependencies legible but can become long. Complex bookings may need a staged flow with a persistent review summary; that behavior was not observed upstream.

entries.title: Featured assortment
suitableFor: A curator has a defensible reason to feature one of three objects.
All displayed objects have meaningful supplied imagery and prices.
avoid: Equal-weight comparisons where one large tile would imply an unsupported ranking.
Missing products or placeholder imagery used to complete the shape.
entries.narrow: Observed grid stacks at small widths. Proposed: preserve an intentional featured-first order and repeat identity/price on each item without relying on overlay contrast.
states: Proposed: fewer than three available objects
Proposed: image unavailable with honest text fallback
Proposed: detail and retained browse return
artDirection: Use unequal image area only when editorial priority is real, while keeping the same identity and price treatment.
Choose crops that preserve the distinguishing product feature; a larger tile must not merely magnify empty background.
entries.tradeoff: A weighted assortment creates an editorial lead at the cost of equal comparison. A regular grid is preferable when customers must compare peers.

entries.title: Document with two maps
suitableFor: A large reference corpus needs both cross-document navigation and in-page wayfinding.
Readers often arrive directly at a specific section.
avoid: Short articles that gain little from two navigation regions.
Overlong navigation that dominates the reading column.
entries.narrow: Proposed: collapse corpus navigation into a named menu and place a compact section index before the article. Anchor destinations need visible headings and navigation-aware scroll space.
states: Proposed: menu close and focus return
artDirection: Limit prose width while giving navigation smaller, quieter type because the article remains the primary object.
Differentiate corpus labels from local headings through alignment and spacing, rather than competing color systems.
entries.tradeoff: Two maps improve orientation in a large corpus but consume width and attention. A single contents list is often sufficient for a small guide.

entries.title: Procedure thread
suitableFor: Actions must happen in order and each has local explanation or evidence.
A reader benefits from returning to a named step.
avoid: Unordered concepts presented as steps purely for decoration.
Implying completion tracking from a numbered document.
entries.narrow: Proposed: keep markers outside the readable text measure and examples inside their step. Long code or tables need their own labelled overflow region.
states: Proposed: direct link to a step
Proposed: unexpected result and recovery guidance
Proposed: completed document with next action
artDirection: Use numbers because order changes the outcome; connect markers lightly enough that they do not overpower instructions.
Give examples and expected results a consistent inset because users compare what they did with what should happen.
entries.tradeoff: A procedure makes order explicit but can hide the larger conceptual model. Include context when a reader must choose among methods rather than follow one.

entries.title: Reading with evidence margin
suitableFor: A claim needs a nearby diagram, source or qualification.
Readers alternate between narrative and close inspection.
avoid: Decorative margin fragments with no relationship to the prose.
Unsupported claims disguised as authoritative annotations.
entries.narrow: Proposed adaptation: place each evidence figure and note immediately after its referenced paragraph when a margin cannot fit. Keep caption, source and limitation with the figure.
states: Proposed: saved place and resumed reading
artDirection: Use a distinct reading face for prose and a restrained annotation style because narrative and evidence have different roles.
Anchor every margin note to a named figure or claim; spacing makes the correspondence visible without invented ornament.
entries.tradeoff: The upstream source supports a reading column and local map, not evidence annotations or saved-place behavior. The proposed margin increases inspection space but interrupts narrative rhythm.

entries.title: Query and result field
suitableFor: A query reduces a collection of visually distinguishable objects.
Each result has a meaningful identity and detail destination.
avoid: Attribute-heavy records that are easier to compare in rows.
Inferring faceted filtering or retained scroll from a search page alone.
entries.narrow: Observed grid reduces to one column. Proposed: retain the query and count before results; restore query and a useful return location after detail.
states: Observed in source: no results message
Proposed: loading, failure and retained return
artDirection: Keep identity and the distinguishing attribute in the same position on every result because the eye scans repeated roles.
Use equal visual area for peer objects so ranking comes from labelled relevance rather than accidental size.
entries.tradeoff: A grid supports visual discovery but exposes fewer comparable attributes. An indexed list can be better for material, dimension or date comparison.

entries.title: Hierarchy with current path
suitableFor: A stable collection has meaningful parent-child relationships.
A visitor needs to know both the current item and nearby alternatives.
avoid: Inventing taxonomy for a small flat collection.
Deep trees whose collapsed state hides the current item.
entries.narrow: Proposed: expose the current path before content and put the full collection in a named expandable region. Restore focus to its trigger on close.
artDirection: Use indentation only for real ancestry; pair it with group labels so hierarchy remains understandable without spatial cues.
Reserve stronger weight for the current destination, leaving siblings readable and comparable.
entries.tradeoff: The inspected wrapper delegates hierarchy rendering to another component; group behavior and keyboard handling were not verified. A flat alphabetical index is often faster for known-item lookup.

entries.title: Choice index
suitableFor: Several peer routes can be distinguished by concise purpose and audience.
Visitors choose what to inspect next rather than complete a transaction.
avoid: Identical vague descriptions that do not help a choice.
Staggering layout when strict row comparison matters.
entries.narrow: Observed grid becomes one column. Proposed: preserve a stable source order and use the same descriptive fields for each route; avoid a stagger when it breaks comparison.
states: Proposed: unavailable route labelled in place
Proposed: filtered empty state and reset
artDirection: Use a compact title and one useful distinction per destination because the visitor is comparing routes, not reading full articles.
Keep repeated entries on a common baseline; reserve any asymmetry for real editorial priority.
entries.tradeoff: The source provides a grid container, not search, destination copy or state handling. A plain linked list is more efficient when titles alone distinguish the choices.
